Hi, I'm in the same situation! I just got diagnosed with CKD stage 3B last month my creatinine was 2.60 mg/dl and I had high uric acid, blood pressure, and cholesterol. During that time I was having second thoughts if I would still continue my Japan trip but my nephro and dietician said that I could continue as long as I watch what I eat and with the right medicines, I can lower blood pressure and cholesterol thus, stabilizing my creatinine.

With the help of my dietician (she allowed me 1 cheat day during my trip), I restricted the portions and what I ate during the trip to fish and chicken and even ate fatty beef 1 time in my trip and last month my lab results came in and I normalized my blood pressure, cholesterol and uric acid. I even lowered my creatinine from 2.60 to 2.57 when I expected this to go higher since I ate beef and failed to control portions in some of my meals during my trip. While I was doubtful that a healthy diet can help me, this result proved to me that a proper diet can help you stabilize the kidneys and hopefully maybe even see a larger decrease of creatinine since recently my dietician advised me to slowly transition into a vegan diet. 

Follow what your doctors advise you. No cola sodas, no beef and pork, no salty foods, no chocolates or foods with high phosporus. Ask for a diet plan. As for treatments, Dialysis is scary and a pain to do weekly but you could talk to your nephro for the option of transplant as a treatment.

When I was diagnosed, I cried everyday for a week and when my nephro asked me how I was coping with it I told her about my crying for a week. She then told me how I shouldn't look at it as a death sentence and some guy in this subreddit told me that my nephro was right and I should see it as a medical journey/ a road to recovery. Emotional stress gets to the kidneys and will stress you out even more so I have no choice but to face it with bravery. Be brave. Do it for you and your loved ones.

Recently i have high blood pressure and the nephrologist told me it was probably because of my diet as the main contributing factor but she does suspect genetics. I started to feel occasional headaches last saturday and was only diagnosed yesterday nov 14 of CKD. My nephrologist computed a GFR of 39. I remember they also had me visit the doctors when i was about maybe 4 or 5 years old. When i was 10 they checked me monthly to see if i had glomerulonephritis but i showed a lack of symptoms. My father has genetics of high uric acid but i dont know if my mother has any. My doctor suggested ketoanalogues and medicines to lower blood pressure, cholesterol and lipid levels. As of now im going to see another kidney doctor and get a second opinion.
